name: Shape
first: A view that is an outline, such as a rectangle or a circle, which takes the whole size it is proposed and draws its outline to fit it.

dependsOn.why: A shape returns its outline as a path, built for the rectangle it is given.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The method `path(in:)` builds a path with `move(to:)`, `addLine(to:)`, and `closeSubpath()`, as on the page of Path.

dependsOn.why: A shape is a type that conforms to SwiftUI's shape protocol, which requires one method.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Pennant` conforms to `Shape` by having `path(in:)`, as `Friendly` conforms to `Greeter` by having `greet(name:)`.

dependsOn.why: A shape takes the whole size it is proposed in the steps of layout, and draws its outline in that size.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The renderer proposes 60 by 30 to `Pennant`, as `filler` proposes 300 by 200 to a color on the page of Layout process.

what.is: A shape is a type that conforms to the protocol `Shape`. Its one required method, `path(in:)`, returns its outline for the rectangle it is given, so the same shape can be drawn at any size. A shape is a view: it takes the whole size it is proposed, and SwiftUI draws its outline in that size.
what.afterExample: The shape `Pennant` is a triangle pointing right, from the corners and the middle of the rectangle it gets. The renderer proposes 60 by 30, so SwiftUI gives `path(in:)` a rectangle of 60 by 30, and the pennant fills it.
what.problem: A path has fixed points, so it has one size. A view must fit whatever room it gets, on every screen. A shape describes its outline from the rectangle it gets, so it fits any size.
what.how: In the steps of layout, a shape chooses the whole size it is proposed. SwiftUI then calls `path(in:)` with a rectangle of that size, and draws the path it returns. Apple's documentation says that a shape with no fill or stroke of its own is filled with the foreground color.

when.text: Use a shape for an outline that should fit any frame, such as a pennant, a badge, or a ticket with a notch.
Don't write a shape that SwiftUI already has, such as a rectangle, a rounded rectangle, a circle, or a capsule.

parts.name: The conformance to `Shape`, line 3
parts.text: The colon and the name `Shape` after `Pennant` say that `Pennant` conforms to the protocol `Shape`. Its one requirement is the method `path(in:)`, and with it, a `Pennant` is a view.

parts.name: The method `path(in:)`, lines 4 to 15
parts.text: The method gets `rect`, the rectangle that the shape is drawn in, and returns the outline for it. Lines 6 to 8 read the right edge, the middle, and the bottom of `rect`, and lines 9 to 13 build a triangle from them, so the triangle grows and shrinks with `rect`.

steps.text: Line 19 makes a `Pennant` and a renderer for it, and line 20 proposes 60 by 30, the size on line 18.
Line 21 asks for the image. In the steps of layout, the shape chooses the whole size it is proposed, 60 by 30.
SwiftUI calls `path(in:)` with a rectangle of that size, and line 5 prints {{path(in:) gets (60.0, 30.0)}}.
Lines 6 to 14 build the triangle for that rectangle, to (60, 15) and (0, 30), and return it. SwiftUI fills it.
Line 22 prints the size of the image, the size that the shape chose: {{60 30}}.

end.text: The shape took the size it was proposed, and `path(in:)` drew the pennant to fit that size.
